question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a first-class agent-ID rename contract, and should that contract preserve explicit workspace paths while moving only OpenClaw-owned defaults and requiring typed plugin migration participation?
rationale: The requested behavior changes durable identity, path ownership, recovery, and extension obligations; those semantics cannot be safely inferred from the existing rejection boundary alone.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow rename contract
options.body: Approve a core-owned journaled rename operation with explicit-path preservation, owned-default-path moves, and a typed plugin participation contract.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Keep the strict ownership guard and document that agent IDs are immutable until a broader agent-state migration design is prioritized.

options.title: Limit scope to core state
options.body: Approve only a core-state rename design and explicitly exclude plugin-owned state until a stable extension contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow rename contract
recommendation.body: Approve a core-owned journaled rename operation with explicit-path preservation, owned-default-path moves, and a typed plugin participation contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Adjacent per-agent architecture work in the supplied context makes this the best available low-confidence routing candidate for the contract decision.
